classification.difficultyReason: Constructs examples showing that equal angles or equal sides alone do not make a polygon regular.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw an irregular hexagon with all equal angles.

answer.short: An equiangular hexagon with unequal side lengths, as shown.
answer.worked: One example is the elongated hexagon shown. Each interior angle is $120^{\circ}$, but its horizontal sides are longer than its sloping sides. It is therefore irregular.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4(a); teacher PDF page 48, printed page 423, Section D
spec.description: Unfilled elongated convex hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges and four sloping end edges.
spec.mathematics: Six interior angles are 120 degrees. The two horizontal sides have length 3 in the construction coordinate frame; the four sloping sides have length 1. These construction values are not printed givens.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw an irregular hexagon with all equal sides.

answer.short: An equal-sided hexagon with unequal interior angles, as shown.
answer.worked: One example is the non-convex hexagon shown. All six sides have equal length, but the inward notch has a reflex interior angle while the other interior angles are not reflex. It is therefore irregular.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4(b); teacher PDF page 48, printed page 423, Section D
spec.description: Unfilled non-convex hexagon with a top peak and inward lower notch; coordinates enforce equal side lengths.
spec.mathematics: Each of the six edges has length 1 in the construction coordinate frame. The notch has a 240-degree interior angle, so the interior angles are unequal. These construction values are not printed givens.
